what: Expand Energy is the largest natural gas producer in the United States by volume, formed from the merger of Chesapeake Energy and Southwestern Energy. It drills in the Appalachian and Haynesville shales.
customers: Utilities, industrial users, liquefied natural gas exporters and power generators.
money: production from Appalachia and the Haynesville basin in Louisiana
moat: Haynesville acreage sits close to Gulf Coast LNG export terminals, which gives its gas the shortest route to the highest-priced market.
risks: Natural gas prices are volatile and set earnings
Debt of about $4.6 billion against almost no cash
Gas production can be shut in when prices fall, which it has done before
Pipeline capacity constraints affect realised prices
opportunities: Revenue grew sharply last year as gas prices recovered and the merger completed
Analysts see about 45% upside from current levels
LNG export and data centre power demand are both raising US gas consumption
watch: Realised gas price against benchmark and production volumes.
